newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. pleased with Japan financial services moves.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pleased with Japan financial services moves.

text.p: The United States is "very pleased" with Japan's progress in implementing a 1995 bilateral financial services pact, a U.S. Treasury official said on Wednesday.
"In general, they have done everything they said they would do to implement the agreement...and in several of the areas have gone well beyond the agreement," the U.S. official told reporters.
He was speaking after a day of talks in Tokyo to review progress under the pact and to discuss developments in the two countries' financial regulatory systems.

The U.S. would also like to see greater disclosure of information needed for investors to assess the performance of pension fund managers and investment trust management companies on a comparable basis as well as greater scope for innovation in the securities market, the official said.

The U.S. also reiterated in Wednesday's talks its interest in Japan's planned "Big Bang" financial deregulation by the year 2001 and its view that it was important for authorities to think about how to strengthen the financial system and cope with systemic risk as deregulation proceeded.

The U.S. official said the Treasury Department and the Finance Ministry had agreed to have further dialogue on structural reform issues in both markets and they would meet again in about six months to discuss financial system reforms in Japan and in the United States.

On Japan's planned reform of its Foreign Exchange Law, the U.S. official said: "It is a potentially very significant development and could have a very important impact on the prospects for broader reform of the financial system." But he added it was necessary to see specific regulations and administrative guidance before making a final evaluation.
